findings_and_questions.source_observation: BuildingProgram and public serde BuildingPlan retain storey_height_metres as f32; the displayed orchestration copies the raw field. The vertical-circulation audit divides the stair base and arrival heights by that raw scalar, rounds and casts directly to u16 before finding a storey. The navigation helper separately admits the same kind of plan value as PositiveLength and uses StoreyIndex::from_elevation, which checks quotient finiteness and u16 representability.
findings_and_questions.conditional_case: If a BuildingPlan with zero storey height and a straight stair at zero base reaches vertical circulation, native f32 0/0 yields NaN; Rust float-to-integer cast produces zero. That local path selects level 0 without its own checked height/quotient failure. Finding a storey and other geometric checks are separate. This is language/source reasoning only, not an executed fixture or a claim that the whole audit returns no issues.
findings_and_questions.qualification: Recipe documentation explicitly permits describing unbuildable combinations and states generate rejects unsupported input; no proof of validation sequencing, arbitrary decoded-plan acceptance, external production reachability, later issue-list disposition or safe call of the complete audit is made. The retained f32 may itself be deliberate raw input at an authoring boundary; the issue is whether it reaches a semantic plan and unchecked division under a contract requiring positive height.

thirteen_lenses.producer-propagation: BuildingProgram and BuildingPlan keep raw storey height across orchestration; navigation admits it only at a particular consumer, while vertical circulation divides the raw retained value.
thirteen_lenses.existing-type-owners: PositiveLength owns finite strictly positive metres; StoreyIndex::from_elevation owns checked rounded ordinal conversion. Their use depends on the actual plan and audit policies.
thirteen_lenses.admission-contracts: Private PositiveLength(f32) and checked manual Deserialize enforce finite >0, rejecting both signed zeroes and negatives. Reflect behavior beyond opaque annotation remains unproved.
thirteen_lenses.invariant-operations: No arithmetic or mutation methods appear on PositiveLength itself; consuming division must separately handle tiny positive values, overflow and finite ordinal range.
thirteen_lenses.aggregate-states: Positive height alone does not prove that a classified level is a member of a particular building, nor that stair base/arrival correspond to distinct occupied storeys.
thirteen_lenses.type-ownership: The shared geometry crate owns positive metre values; animation NonnegativeLength and SignedLength intentionally admit larger sets. Same f32 storage is not automatic owner duplication.
thirteen_lenses.redundant-authority: Program-to-plan copy represents a producer handoff; whether retained program and plan become conflicting independently updated authorities depends on lifecycles not inspected.
thirteen_lenses.behavior-preservation: A future change must preserve valid positive finite values including tiny subnormals, zero-permitting unrelated lengths, zero cadence and rounded-station policy unless the actual owner chooses otherwise.
thirteen_lenses.enum-shapes: No semantic boolean or adjacent variant payload is present in assigned positive-length scalar. Building plan and stair enums require separate source review.
thirteen_lenses.derivability: Manual Deserialize invokes the positive constructor; a plain transparent derived deserialize would require independent evidence of equivalent admission. Existing Serialize/PartialOrd derives do not by themselves prove native reflect behavior.
thirteen_lenses.granularity: Positive length, nonnegative length, signed distance, and positive duration have different sign or unit contracts; widening a positive length to signed/nonnegative is safe at that conversion but may lose proof when a later divisor requires positivity.
thirteen_lenses.magic-strings: Assigned file contains documentation and typed error-to-Serde presentation, not an identified hidden string protocol. Audit messages are native diagnostics; their stability and recipients are not established.
thirteen_lenses.magic-numbers: 0.0 is the intrinsic positive boundary and not an arbitrary gameplay minimum; f32 and u16 numerical operations belong to the storey/cadence kernels and require explicit caller policies, not blind literal replacement.
